DrainageAreaClass.notes: Watershed drainage area class. Breakpoints 10 and 100 km2 are fixed constants.
DrainageAreaClass.rationale: Drainage area is the primary scaling variable for channel geometry, discharge and assemblage composition. 10 km2 separates headwaters from wadeable small streams; 100 km2 separates small streams from larger wadeable rivers. Both are conventional round-number breaks in NRSA and NHDPlus practice, not sample quantiles.

ChannelSlopeClass.notes: Reach channel slope class. Breakpoints 0.5 and 2 percent are fixed constants.
ChannelSlopeClass.rationale: Channel slope controls stream power, substrate sorting and channel type. 0.5 and 2 percent are the conventional low gradient, moderate and steep breaks used in Rosgen-family and Montgomery-Buffington channel typing. National median slope is near 0.13 percent, so this ladder is eligible in roughly half of L3 ecoregions; it is screened where it qualifies and excluded with a recorded reason where it does not.

ElevationClass.notes: Mean watershed elevation class. Breakpoints 300 and 1000 m are fixed constants.
ElevationClass.rationale: Elevation proxies thermal regime, precipitation phase and growing season length. 300 and 1000 m are conventional lowland, upland and montane breaks. Within a single ecoregion this often collapses to two populated classes, which the eligibility screen handles.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 3 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 19 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 4 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The response to landscape pressure is estimated nationally and this ecoregion's own level is added, because the ecoregion holds too few streams clean enough to observe reference condition directly. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 13 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

config.notes: NRSA benthic macroinvertebrate multimetric index (0 to 100); higher is better. EPA's Wadeable Streams Assessment MMI of six metrics scored per NARS-9 region, the same index in every survey cycle; EPA's own condition benchmarks are the published criterion it can be scored against.

config.caveat: Specific conductance carries natural carbonate geology as well as disturbance: a pristine stream in a calcareous valley can score low on this curve.
config.notes: Specific conductance; higher indicates ionic disturbance (worse).
Total nitrogen; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse). The total fraction, reported in every NRSA cycle, and the fraction published nitrogen criteria are written against.
Total phosphorus; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse).
Turbidity; higher indicates more suspended sediment (worse).

NRSA fish multimetric index (0 to 100); higher is better. Eight metrics per NARS-9 region, several adjusted for watershed area, scored from an electrofishing sample; sites sampled by seining carry no index.
Percent of native fish individuals classed tolerant (TOLERANCE_NRSA); higher is worse. Dominance by tolerant fish is a standard multimetric-index component of disturbance.
Large woody debris volume per 100 m; higher is better.
Channel sinuosity; higher generally indicates a more natural planform.

config.caveat: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.
config.notes: Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. Scored because flow alteration and withdrawal also move it.
